summary: The design should preserve the existing lifecycle pipeline, but its attribution and persistence contracts are currently incomplete. The largest risks are duplicate attempt accounting, in-memory loss across processes, cache/cost data being discarded before normalization, and high-cardinality metric labels.

suggestions.title: Carry one explicit attribution object through dispatch and lifecycle events
suggestions.rationale: Attribution is currently split across `DispatchLabels`, `usage_attribution()` ContextVars, `AttemptUsageRow`, and engine-local `attempt_uid`/`execution_id`. `DispatchLabels` lacks feature, execution, and attempt identity, while `UsageRecord` only carries run/seat fields. Introduce one immutable attribution model created by the engine and attach it to every client/dispatcher usage event; keep ContextVars only as a compatibility fallback.

suggestions.title: Put attribution on the event, not only in the subscriber ContextVar
suggestions.rationale: `UsageRecordingSubscriber` reads `current_run_id` and `current_seat` when handling the event, whereas lifecycle events are also forwarded across isolated registries and some emission paths are fire-and-forget. The existing client code already documents that ContextVars must be captured at event construction time. Add explicit attribution fields to `AfterClientCallEvent` and `ClientCallFailedEvent`, so delayed or cross-registry delivery cannot attach a call to the wrong task.

suggestions.title: Aggregate failure markers by attempt_uid instead of treating them as cycles
suggestions.rationale: The Claude dispatcher emits one harvested usage event and then a separate `ClientCallFailedEvent` for a failed dispatch. `RunLedgerRecorder.by_seat()` currently counts every record as a cycle, so one failed attempt becomes two cycles and can inflate failure/round totals. Require `attempt_uid` plus a record phase/type, then aggregate all records for one attempt before reporting.

suggestions.title: Make the authoritative store durable or narrow the CLI guarantee
suggestions.rationale: `RunLedgerRecorder` is explicitly in-memory and its `aclose()` is a no-op, while both the subscriber and recorder intentionally swallow write failures. A separate `wikitoolkit usage report` process cannot read this ledger, and a worker restart loses all records. Either extend the existing durable `CoderTelemetrySink` as the canonical usage store or define a durable usage file with recovery/partial markers; otherwise the stated CLI and cross-process reporting goal is not achievable.

suggestions.title: Normalize cache counters and provider cost before fan-out
suggestions.rationale: `CompletionUsage` preserves provider cache fields mainly inside `extra_usage`; `AfterClientCallEvent` carries only flat input/output counters and a scalar cost; and `CostCalculator` accepts only cached-input tokens. The Claude dispatcher extracts cache counts and `total_cost_usd` but `_emit_usage_event()` currently drops them. Add a provider-neutral usage snapshot to the event/record, pass provider-reported cost when authoritative, and retain the single origin computation rule rather than recalculating in subscribers.

suggestions.title: Keep attempt and execution IDs out of metric labels
suggestions.rationale: `MetricsSubscriber` enforces a cardinality whitelist, but the proposed key includes per-attempt `attempt_uid` and `execution_id`, which are effectively unbounded. Put feature/task/seat dimensions only where their bounded cardinality is demonstrated; expose attempt and execution identity through span attributes, exemplars, logs, or the durable usage store. Add a series-cardinality regression test before changing the metric schema.

suggestions.title: Use a dedicated Codex usage codec, not the generic shared dispatcher module
suggestions.rationale: The generic `_shared.py` module is used by many dispatcher siblings, while Codex-specific parsing already exists as `_usage_from_event()` in the OpenAI client package. Move that logic into a provider-neutral or Codex-specific codec with fixture coverage for terminal, nested, missing, and repeated usage events; have the dispatcher aggregate exactly one terminal usage observation. This avoids coupling all dispatchers to Codex schema details and avoids importing a client implementation merely to parse CLI output.

suggestions.title: Treat Claude Code OTLP ingestion as an opt-in reconciliation source
suggestions.rationale: The repository settings currently install only a `PreToolUse` hook, and the installer is hard-coded to merge that hook. External Claude telemetry therefore has an operational and privacy activation step, in addition to the unresolved sub-agent join contract. Make in-process harvested usage the primary source for the native Claude dispatcher; gate OTLP ingestion behind explicit configuration and require replay fixtures proving the join before making it part of the correctness acceptance criteria.

suggestions.title: Version the price source on every computed cost
suggestions.rationale: Pricing entries contain `valid_from`, but `CostCalculator.cost_usd()` ignores it and uses the currently loaded model price. The module-level cache and override merge can therefore change the answer for historical records after a pricing refresh. Store a pricing revision or content hash and effective interval with the origin-computed cost, and test historical calls against multiple price versions.
